title: Floor 2 Field Kit
unlockCriteria: Defeat your first enemy on Floor 2.
details: Unlock when you defeat your first enemy on Floor 2 to receive a starter equipment piece.
directorFlavor: The prop department scraped together a starter kit from the discount bin. One piece, guaranteed Common quality, exactly the kind of inventory-management busywork the audience adores.

title: Floor 2 Second Wind
unlockCriteria: Defeat 10 enemies on Floor 2.
details: Unlock by defeating 10 enemies on Floor 2 to receive a Common-or-Uncommon equipment piece.
directorFlavor: The audience is warming up. So is the prop budget — this one might actually be Uncommon.

title: Floor 2 Veteran Cast
unlockCriteria: Defeat 30 enemies on Floor 2.
details: Unlock by defeating 30 enemies on Floor 2 to receive an Uncommon-or-Common equipment piece.
directorFlavor: You've earned top billing. The prop department's best (non-Rare) offering awaits.

title: Making Friends
unlockCriteria: Get one Floor 2 family to Friendly standing.
details: Unlock when at least one present Floor 2 family reaches the Friendly relationship band.
directorFlavor: One family actually likes you. Not ‘tolerates,’ not ‘hasn't ordered a hit yet’ — likes. Our focus groups are stunned; they had the under on this at zero. Keep it up and we might have to invent a new sponsorship category.

title: Inner Circle
unlockCriteria: Get two Floor 2 families to Friendly standing at once.
details: Unlock when at least two present Floor 2 families are simultaneously at the Friendly relationship band.
directorFlavor: Two families, both Friendly, both convinced you're on their side. Diplomatically this is either genius or a house of cards waiting for one bad trash-pull. The writers' room has already drafted three betrayal arcs just in case. Sponsors love a coalition; they love the collapse even more.

title: Court Favorite
unlockCriteria: Get every present Floor 2 family to Friendly standing simultaneously.
details: Unlock when every family present on Floor 2 is simultaneously at the Friendly relationship band.
directorFlavor: Every family on the floor, Friendly, all at once. Somewhere the actuaries who model contestant survival odds just quietly deleted a spreadsheet. This isn't supposed to be possible — the whole territory system assumes at least one grudge is always active. We're airing it anyway, because it's genuinely the strangest thing we've filmed all season, and because the sponsors insisted the trophy segment needed a real underdog story that isn't about dying. Enjoy the goodwill; the writers are already looking for a reason to end it.

title: Burned a Bridge
unlockCriteria: Drive one Floor 2 family to Hate standing.
details: Unlock when at least one present Floor 2 family reaches the Hate relationship band.
directorFlavor: One family officially hates your guts. The territory patrols will remember this. Honestly, half the production crew was rooting for a little chaos this episode — congratulations, you delivered.

title: Most Wanted
unlockCriteria: Drive two Floor 2 families to Hate standing at once.
details: Unlock when at least two present Floor 2 families are simultaneously at the Hate relationship band.
directorFlavor: Two families want you dead at the same time, and neither one is willing to wait in line. This is the exact scenario the family-AI team warned us was 'theoretically survivable.' The territory director is having the time of its life reassigning patrols. Legal has asked us to stop calling this segment 'the gauntlet,' so we're calling it 'audience favorite content' instead. Either way, sleep with one eye open, and maybe don't linger near the contested resource.

title: Double Agent
unlockCriteria: Attack a family that considered you Friendly.
details: Unlock the first time you attack a family after it reached the Friendly relationship band with you.
directorFlavor: You waited until they trusted you, then you swung anyway. That's not strategy, that's a season arc. The betrayed family's grudge is now permanent, the writers' room gave you a nickname we can't say on a family-friendly broadcast, and somewhere a sponsor just doubled their ad buy for the reunion episode.

title: Meet the Boss
unlockCriteria: Enter a family's boss den.
details: Unlock the first time you engage a family boss encounter in its den.
directorFlavor: You found the den, and the den found you back. Whether you walk out is a separate achievement entirely — this one's just for showing up.

title: Den Breaker
unlockCriteria: Defeat one family boss.
details: Unlock when you defeat your first Floor 2 family boss.
directorFlavor: One family boss down, decapitated in the most literal sense our compliance department allows us to say on air. The territory board just lost a name. Don't get comfortable — the remaining families noticed, and they have opinions.

title: Den Crusher
unlockCriteria: Defeat two family bosses.
details: Unlock when you defeat two Floor 2 family bosses in the same run.
directorFlavor: Two family bosses, two vacant thrones. The remaining families are recalculating whether ‘diplomacy’ is suddenly a better strategy than ‘territorial aggression.’ Our writers were hoping for a longer power struggle, but a well-timed decapitation makes for great television regardless. The territory map redraws itself in real time now, and frankly, so does our production budget for the finale.

title: Family Annihilator
unlockCriteria: Defeat three or more family bosses.
details: Unlock when you defeat three or more Floor 2 family bosses in the same run.
directorFlavor: Three family bosses, and counting. There is no territory board left to redraw — you redrew it with a body count. The remaining families, if any are left standing at all, have stopped sending patrols and started sending prayers. Our legal team wants it on record that this was not the intended difficulty curve for this floor; the balance team insists it absolutely was. Either way, the audience numbers for this segment are the best we've had all season, and the sponsors are already asking whether you'll do it again next week. You won't. Nobody does this twice.

title: Civilization, Sort Of
unlockCriteria: Find the Floor 2 settlement.
details: Unlock by completing the quest to locate the Floor 2 settlement.
directorFlavor: You found the one patch of this floor with a roof, a bar, and people who won't immediately try to kill you. Production insisted the settlement have working lighting; the caves budget did not survive the negotiation.

title: Meet the Broker
unlockCriteria: Complete the Broker's introduction at the settlement.
details: Unlock once you finish the Broker's introduction dialogue at the settlement.
directorFlavor: You've met the Broker, the settlement's resident middleman for information nobody asked for and favors nobody wanted. Their intro monologue runs long by design — the contract stipulates full screen time regardless of how impatient you look.

title: Found the Way Out
popupText: New achievement: Found the Way Out!
unlockCriteria: Unlock the Floor 2 exit staircase.
details: Unlock once the Floor 2 exit staircase becomes accessible.
directorFlavor: The exit is open. Nobody's making you use it yet — the trash mobs still need thinning, the families still need managing, and frankly the ratings are better while you're still down here. But the door's unlocked, and that's worth something. Consider it a professional courtesy from a production that does, occasionally, want you to survive.

title: Off This Floor
unlockCriteria: Complete the quest to leave Floor 2 and descend the staircase.
details: Unlock by completing the leave-floor quest and confirming descent past Floor 2.
directorFlavor: You did it — diplomacy, decapitation, or a healthy mix of both, and you're still standing at the bottom of the stairs looking up. The family politics reset behind you like nothing happened, which is either merciful or deeply insulting depending on how much blood you spilled to get here. The production team has already started scouting Floor 3 for hazards; you get maybe one commercial break to enjoy this. The reunion special will absolutely bring up whichever family you betrayed. It always does. Enjoy the descent while it lasts.

title: Two-Front War
unlockCriteria: Fight trash mobs from two different families.
details: Unlock once you've landed player-attributed trash kills against two different Floor 2 families.
directorFlavor: Two families' worth of trash mobs, and neither faction seems to have noticed the other one is also mad at you. Efficient, if not exactly diplomatic. The territory director loves this — it means the patrol routes are finally earning their keep.

title: Total War
unlockCriteria: Fight trash mobs from three different families.
details: Unlock once you've landed player-attributed trash kills against three different Floor 2 families.
directorFlavor: Three families' worth of trash mobs on your kill sheet, simultaneously. At this point you're not picking fights so much as running your own private war on multiple fronts, and the territory system is straining to keep the patrol maps updated in real time. The good news is nobody's coordinating against you yet. The bad news is that's exactly the kind of thing that changes the moment we cut to commercial.

title: Scorched Earth
unlockCriteria: Fight trash mobs from four or more different families.
details: Unlock once you've landed player-attributed trash kills against four or more Floor 2 families.
directorFlavor: Every family on the floor has trash-mob blood on the ledger with your name attached. There is no faction left to make peace with, no territory left uncontested, no patrol route that doesn't have you flagged as a threat. The relationship system's tuning docs did not model a contestant hostile to literally everyone at once — we checked. The audience adores this kind of scorched-earth run precisely because it's unsustainable; someone always has to actually win the floor eventually, and right now that someone is doing it the hard way.

title: Safe Harbor
unlockCriteria: Take shelter in a Floor 2 safe room.
details: Unlock the first time you're inside a Floor 2 safe room.
directorFlavor: Four walls, no families, no trash mobs, no minimap dread. It won't last — nothing on this floor lasts — but the production insurance department insists we acknowledge every safe room the moment you find one.

title: Suited Up
unlockCriteria: Unlock the equipment system on Floor 2.
details: Unlock once the equipment system is available to you on Floor 2.
directorFlavor: Slots, sockets, and stat rolls, all yours now. The wardrobe department is thrilled to finally have something to do besides hand out starter gear.

title: Pocket Change
unlockCriteria: Carry 150 gold.
details: Unlock once your gold balance reaches 150.
directorFlavor: 150 gold, burning a hole in your inventory. The sponsors would like to remind you the Quartermaster accepts all major currencies, including the ones you looted off corpses.

title: Comfortable
unlockCriteria: Carry 300 gold.
details: Unlock once your gold balance reaches 300.
directorFlavor: 300 gold and no immediate plans to spend it. The finance department is impressed; the writers are bored — hoarding doesn't make good television, but the sponsors love a contestant with liquidity. Keep it up and the Quartermaster might start recognizing you by name instead of by threat level.

title: Deep Pockets
unlockCriteria: Carry 500 gold.
details: Unlock once your gold balance reaches 500.
directorFlavor: 500 gold in reserve, sitting there unspent while the Quartermaster's stock rotates past you. Somewhere a production accountant is quietly furious that a contestant is out-saving the actual sponsors. We'd call this fiscal responsibility if we thought for one second you planned it that way. Either way, the number's real, the gold is yours, and the audience loves watching a hoard get bigger even when nothing happens with it.

title: New Tricks
unlockCriteria: Unlock 2 abilities.
details: Unlock once you've unlocked 2 passive abilities.
directorFlavor: Two abilities unlocked, and the skill tree finally looks like it's going somewhere. The stunt coordinators appreciate the extra options; it means fewer boring fight loops for the highlight reel.

title: Growing Arsenal
unlockCriteria: Unlock 3 abilities.
details: Unlock once you've unlocked 3 passive abilities.
directorFlavor: Three abilities deep now, and the fight choreography team has officially run out of excuses to call your kit 'basic.' Sponsors are asking whether the next one comes with a cooldown they can put on a billboard. Probably.

title: Loaded Toolkit
unlockCriteria: Unlock 5 abilities.
details: Unlock once you've unlocked 5 passive abilities.
directorFlavor: Five abilities unlocked, which is roughly four more than the balance team was comfortable with when they first sketched this floor. The kit's genuinely versatile now — there's a build-of-the-week segment forming in the edit bay whether you asked for one or not. The families have started adjusting their tactics around whatever you've been doing, which is either flattering or a very bad sign depending on how the next den goes. Either way, the production loves a contestant who can no longer be summarized in one sentence.

title: Sharpened Edge
unlockCriteria: Reach skill level 8 in any skill.
details: Unlock once any single skill reaches level 8.
directorFlavor: Level 8 in a single skill is the kind of specialization our balance team keeps insisting isn't achievable this early. And yet here we are, watching one skill line do most of the actual work while the rest of your kit rides along for the highlight reel. The families have noticed the pattern too — the smart ones are already adjusting their approach angles. We'd tell you to diversify, but frankly the ratings prefer a contestant with one terrifyingly good trick over five mediocre ones. Keep sharpening.

title: Built Different
unlockCriteria: Spend 10 stat points.
details: Unlock once you've spent 10 stat points.
directorFlavor: Ten stat points committed, no refunds, no regrets we're aware of. The character sheet is starting to look like a build someone actually planned instead of clicked at random. The sponsors appreciate a contestant who invests; the writers appreciate that it gives them something concrete to point at when the next fight goes suspiciously well.

title: Body Count of the Season
popupText: New achievement: Body Count of the Season!
unlockCriteria: Defeat 60 enemies across the run.
details: Unlock once your cumulative run-wide kill count reaches 60, tracked across every floor you've cleared.
directorFlavor: 60 kills and climbing, tallied across every floor you've touched this run — rats, slimes, trash mobs, the works. The season highlight reel is going to need its own editor at this rate. Nobody's counting the ones that got away; we only track the ones who didn't.

title: Hoarder's Ledger
unlockCriteria: Carry 800 gold at once, at any point in the run.
details: Unlock once your gold balance reaches 800 at any point in the current run.
directorFlavor: 800 gold, all yours, all at once. The Quartermaster's accountants have started a betting pool on whether you'll ever actually spend it. The production would like to remind sponsors that hoarding is not, in fact, a strategy we designed for — it's just what happens when a contestant refuses to buy anything nice for themselves.

title: Two-Floor Gauntlet
unlockCriteria: Clear two floors in the same run.
details: Unlock once you've cleared two separate floors within the current run.
directorFlavor: Two floors cleared, same contestant, same run, no do-overs. The production loves this one specifically because it can't be gamed — you either survived the transition or you didn't. Floor 1's rats and Floor 2's families have nothing in common except that you outlasted both. That's the whole achievement, really: you're still here.

title: Skill of the Season
popupText: New achievement: Skill of the Season!
unlockCriteria: Reach skill level 10 in any skill, at any point in the run.
details: Unlock once any single skill reaches level 10 at any point during the current run.
directorFlavor: Level 10 in one skill, run-wide, no floor reset to hide behind. The stunt team has officially built a highlight package around whatever you've been doing with it. Sponsors want the naming rights. We haven't decided if we're selling them yet, but the number's real, and so is the reputation you've built with it.

title: Fully Outfitted
unlockCriteria: Unlock the equipment system, tracked for the rest of the run.
details: Unlock once the equipment system is available and stays flagged for the remainder of the current run.
directorFlavor: Equipment unlocked, and it's staying unlocked for the rest of the run — no floor transition takes this away from you. The wardrobe department considers this the real season premiere.

title: Ability Collector
unlockCriteria: Unlock 6 abilities across the run.
details: Unlock once you've unlocked 6 passive abilities at any point in the current run.
directorFlavor: Six abilities collected over the course of the run, run-wide and floor-agnostic. At this point the fight choreography team has stopped trying to predict what you'll do next and started just filming everything. The season's build-diversity metrics have never looked better, and frankly neither has our highlight reel.
